clue.text: Move towards men, going with the flow

indicators.note: move tells us to shift the letters of the following words around into a new order

explanation.surface: An instruction to edge closer to some men while drifting along with the crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Move' looks like a verb of travel but signals rearranging the ten letters of TOWARDS MEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Travelling in the direction a river's current runs is literally going with its flow.

clue.text: County ultimately unprepared, or ready?

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word unprepared

parts.note: taken as written
set means ready, as in 'ready, steady, go'

explanation.surface: A question of whether a county is caught unprepared or is fully ready.
explanation.walkthrough: DORSET is a county on the south coast of England.
explanation.definitionFit: Dorset is one of the shires of southern England, an example of a county.

clue.text: Good and evil

definitions.meaning: in slang, something excellent or cool is described this way
the usual sense: morally bad, sinful

explanation.surface: A pairing of opposites, good and evil.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is slang for excellent and also, in its standard sense, a synonym for wrongdoing.

clue.text: Aspect ain't so shabby in out-of-this-world accommodation

indicators.note: shabby suggests something knocked about and out of shape, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A defence of some unusual lodgings: their appearance is not as run-down as people claim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shabby' signals an anagram of ASPECT AIN'T SO.
explanation.definitionFit: An orbiting habitat for astronauts is literally lodging beyond our planet, so beyond this world.

clue.text: Run and help Sally?

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for a run
aid means help

explanation.surface: Someone is told to run and assist a woman called Sally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sally' looks like a woman's name but is a sortie, a sudden military attack; the question mark flags the disguise.
explanation.definitionFit: A sally is a sudden sortie or attack out of a besieged position, much like a sudden incursion.

clue.text: As are a number of clones, despite what you say

definitions.text: As are a number of clones
definitions.meaning: clones are identical, each one just like the others
nevertheless, even so, in spite of your objection

explanation.surface: A retort to someone claiming clones differ: they are identical regardless.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes identical copies and is also an idiom meaning nevertheless or regardless.

clue.text: Place tug behind ship at the outset

indicators.note: behind puts the word for tug after the ship's letter
at the outset means take just the opening letter of the word ship

parts.note: to tow is to tug or pull along

explanation.surface: A harbour instruction to fix a tug boat behind a ship at the start of a voyage.
explanation.definitionFit: To stow something is to put it away or place it carefully, a direct synonym of the verb place.

clue.text: German not cute, I gathered

indicators.note: gathered suggests the letters are collected up and assembled afresh in another order

explanation.surface: Someone concludes that a German person is not cute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gathered' looks like 'I understood' but signals an anagram of NOT CUTE I.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes things relating to the Germanic peoples, so it can stand for German.

clue.text: Very large part of building housing journalist

indicators.note: housing means the first piece holds the second inside it

parts.note: a wing is a section extending from a main building
a hack is a journalist, often a disparaging term

explanation.surface: A huge section of a building has a journalist living in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Very large' is British informal usage, as in 'a whacking great bill'.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal British usage for enormous, describing something of great size.

clue.text: A note in film music of the Fifties?

indicators.note: in places the second piece inside the first

parts.note: Rocky is the 1976 boxing film starring Sylvester Stallone
a bill is a banknote, especially in American usage

explanation.surface: A musical note heard in a film soundtrack from the 1950s.
explanation.walkthrough: 'note' looks musical but means a banknote, a BILL.
explanation.definitionFit: This style blending country and early rock and roll flourished in the 1950s, so it is an example of that decade's music.

clue.text: A little grizzly, possibly, on a Caribbean island

indicators.note: on means the first piece comes before the A in this down-and-across charade, here simply followed by it

parts.note: a grizzly bear's young is a cub; possibly marks it as one example of a cub

explanation.surface: A small bear perhaps found on a tropical island.
explanation.definitionFit: The largest island nation in the Caribbean Sea, an example of an island there.

clue.text: Drunk in recompense for divine existence?

indicators.note: drunk suggests something reeling and jumbled, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Is getting drunk as compensation a heavenly way to live?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drunk' signals an anagram of IN RECOMPENSE.
explanation.definitionFit: Being present everywhere at once is an attribute traditionally ascribed to God, a divine mode of being.

clue.text: Football team score with nine sent off?

definitions.meaning: a side in football has this many players
a score is twenty, and twenty minus nine leaves this number

explanation.surface: A football side scores a goal despite having nine players sent off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'score' and 'sent off' look like football, but score is 20 and nine taken away is the count needed.
explanation.definitionFit: A soccer side fields that many players, so the number is used for the team itself.

clue.text: Actor wearing small diamond, a national symbol

indicators.note: the actor wearing the other pieces means they wrap around him

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
rock is slang for a diamond
a ham is an overacting performer

explanation.surface: A performer sporting a little diamond as an emblem of the nation.
explanation.definitionFit: The three-leaved clover is the emblem of Ireland, an example of a national symbol.

clue.text: Convincing case for highly developed skill

parts.note: a strong argument is a convincing one
a suit is a legal case, a lawsuit

explanation.surface: A persuasive legal argument made in favour of expertise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'case' looks like an argument but is a lawsuit.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom from card games for the thing a person is best at, their particular talent.

clue.text: I insist tact must be deployed to trap a data expert

indicators.note: to trap means the jumbled letters close around the single letter
deployed means arranged in a new way, so these letters are shuffled

explanation.surface: Someone demands that diplomacy be used to catch out an analyst.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deployed' signals an anagram of I INSIST TACT; 'to trap' puts A inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who collects and interprets numerical information professionally is an expert in data.

clue.text: Quartets playing for uninvited resident

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters are moved around freely into a new order

explanation.surface: String quartets performing for someone who turned up uninvited.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone occupying a building without permission or a lease is an unwanted occupant.

clue.text: A few words in time?

definitions.meaning: a short grammatical unit made of several words
time served in prison, a term handed down by a judge

explanation.surface: A brief remark delivered at the right moment.
explanation.definitionFit: A grammatical unit of words, and also the jail term a convict serves, often called time.

clue.text: Suggest the gospel isn't truth? I've just written it!

definitions.meaning: to cast doubt on the second gospel, the book of Mark, is to query Mark
the setter has just put this punctuation symbol at the end of the previous phrase

explanation.surface: A sceptic doubts scripture, then points out the punctuation they have just written.
explanation.walkthrough: The gospel is that of St Mark; doubting it is querying Mark.
explanation.definitionFit: The symbol ending an interrogative sentence, and literally doubting the evangelist Mark.

clue.text: Plain aunt struggling to embrace doctor

indicators.note: to embrace means the jumbled letters wrap around the doctor
struggling suggests the letters thrash about into a new order

explanation.surface: An unglamorous aunt fighting to hug a doctor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plain' looks like an adjective describing the aunt but is the definition, a noun. 'struggling' makes TUNA.
explanation.definitionFit: The treeless Arctic expanse is an example of a vast flat open plain.

clue.text: Suddenly move forward around old room

indicators.note: around means the first piece goes round the second

parts.note: to lunge is to thrust forward suddenly

explanation.surface: Someone darts forward around an old room.
explanation.definitionFit: A sitting room in a house, or a public bar area, is a type of room.

clue.text: While voice filled with hatred at first, I'm disgusted!

indicators.note: filled with means the voice takes the next letter inside it

parts.note: alto is a singing voice

indicators.note: at first takes only the opening letter of hatred

parts.note: ugh is an exclamation of disgust

explanation.surface: A singer full of hatred exclaims in revulsion.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words are conjunctions meaning whereas or even though, introducing a contrast.

clue.text: Fake painting so exquisite, Uffizi didn't object originally

indicators.note: originally means take the first letter of each of the following words

explanation.surface: A forgery so fine that the Uffizi gallery in Florence raised no objection.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means sham or not genuine, a counterfeit, so it matches fake.

clue.text: Try attack

definitions.meaning: to have a go at something is to make an attempt
to knife or lunge at someone with a blade

explanation.surface: An attempt at an assault.
explanation.definitionFit: Means an attempt, as in have a go, and also a knife thrust or assault.

clue.text: In reality, Newcastle's river

indicators.note: in means the letters sit inside the run of words reality and Newcastle's

explanation.surface: A claim about what really is Newcastle's own river.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tyne is the river running through Newcastle upon Tyne, so the clue nearly reads as a whole.
explanation.definitionFit: The waterway of north-east England flowing through Newcastle is an example of a river.

clue.text: Looking for lecturer somewhere in Cambridgeshire

parts.note: hunting means searching or looking for
a don is a university lecturer, especially at Oxford or Cambridge

explanation.surface: Searching for a university teacher somewhere in an English county.
explanation.walkthrough: Huntingdon is a market town in Cambridgeshire, an English county.
explanation.definitionFit: The market town, birthplace of Oliver Cromwell, lies in that eastern English county.

clue.text: Lech returning for a dance

indicators.note: returning means the word for lech is read backwards

parts.note: to lech is to ogle lustfully, to leer

explanation.surface: A lecherous man comes back to ask for a dance.
explanation.definitionFit: A lively Scottish or Irish folk dance, an example of a dance.

clue.text: Colleague heading for breakdown during deadlock

indicators.note: during means the next letter goes inside the word for deadlock

parts.note: stalemate means deadlock, a position where no progress is possible

indicators.note: heading for takes the first letter of breakdown

explanation.surface: A collapse in negotiations during a standoff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading for' looks like 'on the way to' but takes the first letter, B.
explanation.definitionFit: Originally a horse from the same stable, the word now means a colleague or fellow member of an organisation.
